layers.process: Some border villages are in the Protected Area (Third Schedule appendix). In Kinnaur district: Kunnu, Charang, Nesang, Dubling, Dabling, Khab, Namgia, Tashigang, Kaa, Yangthang, Maling, Nako, Maling Dogri and Chango. In Lahaul and Spiti district: Dhankar, Shichiling, Poh, Tabo, Lari, Samdo, Korik, Gue and Hurling. Foreigners need a Protected Area Permit to enter or stay in them. Apply online at indianfrro.gov.in (the e-FRRO portal) or in the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app; the permit is issued electronically. Citizens of Afghanistan, China or Pakistan, and people of origin there (born there, a parent or grandparent born and permanently living there, or ever a citizen), need the central government's prior approval. Smartraveller advises applying at least 4 weeks ahead; entering without a permit carries significant penalties.

layers.process: Listed Tibetan settlements, monasteries, nunneries and institutions are Restricted Areas (Fourth Schedule). They include sites in McLeodganj, Dharamsala and Dharamkot (among them Namgyal Monastery, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, Tushita Meditation Centre and Dhamma Sikhara Vipassana Centre), Sidhpur and Norbulingka, Bir, Tashijong, Rewalsar, Kullu, Manali, Shimla, Dalhousie and Sirmour. Daytime visits are allowed without a permit if the settlement, monastery or institute gives the visitor's name, parentage, date of birth, nationality, passport and visa numbers to the Foreigners Registration Officer. Staying needs a Restricted Area Permit; foreign students can get one valid for 3 years if the institute vouches for them.

laws.rule: A July 2022 Himachal Pradesh notification under the Non-Biodegradable Garbage (Control) Act prohibits people, including traders and vendors, from specified dealings in listed single-use plastic items. The list includes plastic carry bags and disposable plastic or thermocol plates, cups and cutlery. Check current orders and applicable exceptions before travel.

laws.rule: Under the Himachal Pradesh Prohibition of Cow Slaughter Act 1979, section 5, no one may sell or offer to sell beef or beef products in any form, except for prescribed medicinal purposes. Cow includes a bull, bullock, ox, heifer or calf. Beef excludes flesh in sealed containers imported into the State. Section 4A bars exporting cows for slaughter.
laws.penalty_signal: Up to 5 years of rigorous imprisonment, or a fine of up to INR 25,000 (about A$373), or both (section 8(1)). The offence is cognizable and non-bailable.

laws.rule: The Himachal Pradesh Non-Biodegradable Garbage (Control) Act 1995 bars throwing non-biodegradable garbage, or food waste in a plastic bag, into drains (section 3(1)), and bars leaving any garbage in a public place or place open to public view unless it is in a garbage receptacle or at a spot designated by the local authority (section 3(2)).
laws.penalty_signal: Up to 3 months in jail or a fine of up to INR 25,000 (about A$373), or both (section 8(1)); the offence can be compounded for a sum the State sets.

laws.rule: Under the Himachal Pradesh Excise Act 2011, section 18, no one may possess liquor above the limit the State sets under section 25 as the retail-sale limit, except under a licence or a permit or pass granted by the Collector. Moving liquor above a prescribed quantity needs a Collector's pass; a pass from another State may be accepted on conditions. The numeric limits are set by notification, not in the Act.

Under the Himachal Pradesh Excise Act, 2011, no person may allow consumption of liquor at any public place except under a sale licence. Consuming liquor in an unlicensed public place is an offence, with a fine of at least one thousand rupees and up to five thousand rupees. Creating a nuisance in a public place after consuming liquor is an offence, with imprisonment of up to three months and a fine of at least two thousand rupees and up to ten thousand rupees.

A licence holder, or a person acting on the holder's behalf, may not sell or deliver any liquor to a person apparently under 18 (fine of thirty thousand rupees). Employing anyone under 18 in a liquor vend, bar or other place where liquor or other intoxicants are sold, stored or served is an offence, with imprisonment of up to six months or a fine of fifty thousand rupees, or both.

items.text: Under the Himachal Pradesh Excise Act, 2011, a licence holder may not sell or deliver any liquor to a person apparently under 18. Liquor may not be consumed in an unlicensed public place, and creating a nuisance in a public place after drinking is an offence. Possession above the State retail-sale limit needs a licence, permit or pass; the Act itself does not state that quantity.
